- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoots by 5–15% to avoid overreacting.
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model should adjust forecast downward by 3–8% in next 3–5 periods.
- If forecast consistently overestimates early in 30d horizon (e.g., first 5 days), apply a 2–5% downward bias to first 3–4 periods.
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., ±0.3 swings), reduce forecast smoothness — allow ±2–3% deviation from trend to capture noise.
- If forecast peaks after a strong sentiment spike, cap the peak at 1.2x the prior 5-day average to prevent overcorrection.
- If true outcome is below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 periods to avoid “stuck above” bias.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3–0.6), forecast should be anchored to 30d moving average — avoid sharp directional moves unless sentiment confirms trend.
